jobs.title: Finance Transformation Program Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

About The Role

Atoms is building a Finance function where routine work runs on automation and AI, and Finance partners spend their time on judgment, forecasting, and advising the business. As the Finance Transformation Lead, you will turn that vision into a roadmap and then deliver it. You’ll work with Finance, Engineering, Data, and Internal Audit to redesign how we plan, transact, close, and report. You’ll also make sure every change holds up under audit scrutiny.

In the first 6 to 12 months, you’ll own the overall Finance Transformation roadmap, prioritization framework, and KPIs, and personally lead the redesign and automation of Procure-to-Pay, from requisition through payment. You’ll work closely with the Finance Systems and Data Engineering teams to translate process needs into technical requirements, and with other transformation leads to keep the portfolio coordinated. After that, you’ll extend your scope to partner with Strategic Finance on transforming planning, forecasting, and analysis. As the portfolio grows, you’ll help set the strategic direction for Finance Transformation across the organization.

What You’ll Do

Set the direction

Own the multi-year Finance Transformation roadmap with the VP, Finance Technology and Transformation. Tie it to Atoms’ growth plans and the Finance operating model.
Build and run the prioritization framework, business cases, and benefits tracking that decide what we fund. Maintain a single view of the portfolio across Procure-to-Pay, Order-to-Cash, Record-to-Report, and Strategic Finance, including dependencies and capacity.
Define and track program KPIs, such as close cycle time, touchless transaction rate, cost to serve, forecast accuracy, realized savings and capacity released, and stakeholder satisfaction. Report progress to Finance leadership regularly.

Lead Procure-to-Pay transformation

Take a first-principles approach to the end-to-end P2P process, including intake and requisition, sourcing, contracts, purchase orders, receiving, invoice processing, approvals, payment, and vendor management. Fix the process before automating it.
Lead selection and implementation of procurement and AP automation tools with Finance Systems, covering requirements, vendor assessment, build-versus-buy, and total cost of ownership.
Deliver automation in high-volume work such as invoice capture and coding, PO matching, exception handling, and accruals, and define the controls that go with it.

Partner with Strategic Finance (after the first 6 to 12 months)

Work with Strategic Finance and FP&A to redesign planning, budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis processes, and the tools and data behind them.
Identify and deliver automation and AI use cases such as forecast support, variance commentary, and self-serve reporting, working with Finance Data Engineering and the Finance ML/AI team.
Help define the data and metrics foundations that Strategic Finance needs to scale.

Put AI to work, responsibly

Identify and ship practical AI use cases in Finance, including agentic workflows.
Decide, with process owners, which work belongs with people and which with AI.
Establish governance for AI in Finance: human-in-the-loop review, accountability, model validation, documentation, and audit readiness.

Project management and controls

Lead project management for cross-functional initiatives, including scope, timelines, budgets, risks, and change management.
Stay close enough to the work to review process designs, data models, and configurations yourself.
Work with Internal Audit and external auditors early, so controls are designed in and documented rather than added later.

Prepare The Team For What’s Next

Assess how Finance roles and skills will change with automation and AI, and help define new career paths and learning programs.
Lead change management: communication, training, adoption tracking, and feedback loops, so new tools and processes are actually used.
Guide and mentor Finance Transformation specialists and other team members on process, project, and portfolio practices.

What We're Looking For

10 years of progressive experience in Finance, Accounting/Controllership, or FP&A, with at least 5 years in Finance Transformation.
Deep experience in Procure-to-Pay, and a record of delivering measurable results from ERP or procurement system implementations, process redesign, automation, or data modernization.
Experience building a transformation roadmap, prioritization framework, and benefits tracking for a portfolio of initiatives, and reporting on it to senior leaders.
Working knowledge of AI and automation tools, and sound judgment on when and how to apply them in a controlled environment.Strong understanding of controls and financial reporting requirements.
Familiarity with finance platforms such as NetSuite, Oracle, SAP, Workday, Coupa, Anaplan, or similar, and with data tools such as SQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, or BI platforms.Experience leading without direct authority across Finance, Engineering, and Data, and managing external partners.
Clear executive communication, strong analytical skills, and comfort with ambiguity.
Nice to have: experience with FP&A or Strategic Finance processes and planning tools such as Anaplan, Adaptive Planning, or Pigment.

How You’ll Succeed Here

You question “how we’ve always done it” and back your view with data.
You get into the details of a process, a data set, or a system configuration when it matters.
You think about what’s best for Atoms, not for any one team.
You’re curious about new technology and disciplined about controls.
You build trust quickly and keep people moving in the same direction.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What Else You Need To Know

This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

The base salary range for this role is $170,000 - $210,000 per year.

Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package. You may also be eligible for equity awards and an annual performance-based bonus.

Benefits Summary (USA Full-Time Exempt Employees)

Paid Parental Leave

Benefits Are Subject To Change At The Company's Discretion.

Atoms accepts applications on an ongoing basis.

Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?

jobs.description:
About Rivian

Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.

Role Summary

You will lead the end-to-end delivery of IT infrastructure programs for our commercial and workplace build-outs, from site planning through go-live. You will bring structured programs and change management to every site. You will coordinate IT, Facilities, construction partners and vendors so each location opens on time, on budget, and ready for the people using it.

Responsibilities

Program Delivery

Define scope, roles, milestones, and measurable KPIs for each program, and tie them to broader infrastructure goals.
Own each program from initiation to closure across workplace build-outs and infrastructure platform projects.
Build and maintain master program schedules in Jira and Smartsheet. Align deployment windows with construction and operational dependencies.
Manage procurement through Coupa or similar tools: requisitions, vendor engagement, budget tracking, and financial control.
Track risks, issues, and dependencies, and escalate early with clear options.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Translate technical and business requirements into clear reporting for Infrastructure and Facilities leadership.
Align Network, A/V, Desktop Engineering, SRE/DevOps, Facilities PM/Design Manager, the General Contractor, low-voltage and architectural/engineering teams, and external vendors.
Run cross-disciplinary working sessions that resolve conflicts and keep decisions moving.
Apply a structured change management framework for communications, change control, and risk. This keeps disruption low during facilities and technology rollouts.

Automation & Insight

Automate workflows, sync data, and build integrations across Jira, Smartsheet, and Google Workspace.
Use AI tools to build dashboards, reports, and tracking that give leadership real-time visibility.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
4+ years managing complex, cross-functional IT infrastructure projects or programs, preferably in a manufacturing or industrial setting.
Experience working with General Contractors and Facilities teams on commercial or workplace construction.
Working knowledge of structured cabling, Division 27 standards, A/V standards, and telecom and construction drawings for both office and industrial environments.
Proven ability to run programs with schedules, budgets, and procurement in tools such as Jira, Smartsheet, and Coupa.
Scripting or development skills (e.g., Python, Apps Script) to automate workflows and build integrations.
Experience using AI tools to produce dashboards, reporting, and monitoring.
PMP, PgMP, or an organizational change management certification (e.g., Prosci).

Pay Disclosure

The salary range for this role is $84,600 - $105,800 for Palo Alto based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.

The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.

We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Plan if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com.

You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee).

Our interview process is designed to evaluate your personal technical foundation, real-time problem-solving logic, and structured capabilities. Therefore, the use of assistive generative AI tools to formulate or deliver your solutions during live interview sessions is not permitted
. We care most about how you think — how you make sense of unclear requirements, weigh trade-offs, and explain why you chose one approach over another. We value your unique human perspective, your authenticity, and the journey it takes to reach a solution.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Candidate Data Privacy and Technology

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager - Site Lead
jobs.description:
Perkins&Will Science & Technology

Our SF studio, 120+ people inside a 3,000-person global firm, is delivering a state-of-the-art science and technology campus, and we are seeking a Senior Project Manager to serve as site lead. This is the person who sees the whole project at once and keeps every team, consultant, and client stakeholder pointed in the same direction.

You'll be on site regularly, running the coordination that holds a multi-building campus together: a consultant team spanning landscape, site utilities, and field operations; a client with many voices; and a schedule where one building's delay ripples into the next. You need enough technical depth in complex projects to spot a problem early, ask the right questions, and bring in the right expert when appropriate.

What You'll Own

Serve as site lead and the senior on-site representative of the design team, with the authority to convene, coordinate, and escalate.
Oversee the full consultant team, including landscape, civil and site utilities, MEP, structural, process piping, and hold each to scope, schedule, and quality.
Keep all site utilities moving as one project. Manage the interfaces between site utilities, phases, and site infrastructure, so a decision in one place doesn't create a problem somewhere else.
Own the campus-level master schedule and phasing strategy. Work with Project Architects, engineers, client and general contractor representatives to head off schedule conflicts as the project changes.
Ensure documentation considers full coordination of all site utilities, infrastructure, and landscape with building systems, including utility routing, tie-ins, shutdowns, and the campus-wide services that labs depend on.
Facilitate and administer the permitting process for all site-related permits. Review submitted permit drawings and specifications, prepare validation reports summarizing findings, and administer the permit submission, plan-check response, and resubmission process by organizing comments and consolidating responses. Engineers of Record remain responsible for all technical responses, design, and documentation.
Track interfaces between site work and future building projects, including work performed under separate permits or contracts, so nothing falls between permit packages.

Lead senior client management: steering committees, executive updates, and the relationships that keep trust intact when things get hard.
Run the alignment rhythm: Chair the integrated team meetings, coordination reviews, minutes and memos, and decision tracking. You're accountable for timely, complete communication between the client, consultants, contractors, and project team.
Partner with applicable engineers, architects, landscape architects and the contractor on constructability, sequencing, site logistics, and safety, and oversee construction administration through closeout.
Manage risk at the program level. Monitor client and technical issues, surface them early to limit liability, frame options and consequences, and drive them to resolution.
Hold the quality bar high. Make sure documents are reviewed for accuracy, omissions, legibility, and compliance with the firm's Project Delivery Manual.
You will not be executing any documentation of drawings or specifications.

What You'll Bring

Experience:

10 to 15+ years in architecture or design and construction delivery, with significant time as a Senior Project Manager or Senior Project Architect on large, campus-scale or multi-building projects.
Site lead or field leadership experience on projects with multiple concurrent buildings or phases.
Technical depth in complex building facilities a plus: MEP-intensive systems, modular building systems, utility distribution, and specialized environments.
Working knowledge of site infrastructure, civil and utility coordination, and landscape integration.
Experience administering permit submissions and plan-check responses for site, civil, and utility work with local jurisdictions.
Fluency in building codes, life safety requirements, site analysis, specifications, contract documents, and construction contract administration, from project kickoff through closeout.
A track record of leading large consultant teams and holding them accountable.
Familiarity with collaborative delivery models (IPD, TVD, design-build, CM at Risk) is helpful. Deep TVD expertise is not required.

How you lead:

You see the whole board. You hold the big picture without losing track of what's at risk this week.
Calm, credible, and direct with the team, clients, contractors, and consultants.
You build alignment rather than mandate it, and you know when to make the call yourself.
Polished in executive and large stakeholder forums.
You build systems that let others run the details, so you can stay focused on what only you can see.

Software:

Microsoft Project or Smartsheet for master scheduling
Bluebeam Revu
Working knowledge of Revit and BIM coordination tools such as Navisworks or Autodesk Construction Cloud
Procore, Newforma, or similar construction management platforms a plus
Microsoft 365

Credentials:

Bachelor's degree in architecture or a related discipline, required
Architectural license required (or 20 years of project management and design experience)
PMP or equivalent a plus
LEED GA within 6 months of hire

What You'll Get

Salary range: $141,100-$207,300 commensurate with experience, education and skillset.

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) retirement plan and paid time off
Professional development stipend and dedicated continuing education time
Performance-based bonuses
Access to firmwide affinity groups and leadership development programs
Studio initiatives and events; a team that actually likes each other

Our Commitment

Our culture is grounded in a firmwide commitment to Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (JEDI). Not as a tagline, but as how we hire, promote, and build teams. We conduct annual pay equity audits and train all managers on pay practices. We believe inclusion drives creativity.

Blend's software powers mortgage, home equity, and consumer banking for many of the largest banks, credit unions, and lenders in the US. Client Activation is the team that takes a signed customer to a live, working product.

You will own the delivery of our most complex customer engagements: Rapid home lending implementations and dedicated engineering PODs that build alongside our largest customers. You run the plan, the dates, the risks, and the governance, working with our Professional Services Consultants, who own the solution, and with Engineering and Product.

What you bring

Seven or more years managing customer-facing implementations of enterprise SaaS, with several projects running at once.
Experience delivering for banks, credit unions, mortgage lenders, or other regulated financial institutions.
Agile delivery experience alongside engineering teams: sprints, velocity, release planning, and backlog governance.
A record of recovering projects that were off track, with specifics on what you changed.
Executive presence: you run SteerCos, deliver bad news early with options, and hold your ground on scope.

AI-first working habits. You already use AI tools to do real work faster, can show us how, and know where to check their output.

PMP, PMI-ACP, or a similar certification.
Mortgage, home equity, or loan origination domain knowledge.
Experience with TaskRay on Salesforce.
Experience with dedicated development team or co-build engagements governed by a SOW.
Hands-on experience building internal automations or AI workflows.

Why you might want this role

Ownership of the engagements that matter most to our customers and to Blend, with a direct line to the Vice President, Client & Revenue Operations.
Clear, visible impact: projects that go live on time.
A new function you help shape, with AI-first tooling already in place.

About CEA CAPA

At CEA CAPA, we believe studying and interning abroad is a transformative experience. By immersing themselves in new cultures, our students gain valuable skills and perspectives that shape their futures.

We’re proud to be a recognized sector leader, known for our delivery of impactful academic, professional and cultural experiences. This is achieved through our dedicated global team who provide comprehensive guidance, instruction, support and resources to maximize the benefit of our students’ time abroad.

A sense of belonging is central to CEA CAPA’s mission. We foster a work environment that values diversity and is free from bias. Our hiring practices are based on professional qualifications, skills and competence.

With a footprint that spans 53 cities in 20 countries across Europe, Latin America and Australia our 450 strong global workforce deliver exceptional cultural experiences abroad to over 7,000 students per year.

Position Summary

Custom Program Management is a fast-paced, goal-oriented unit within CEA CAPA Education Abroad. The Custom Program Manager is responsible for collaborating with CEA CAPA’s USA based and international staff along with CEA CAPA’s institutional partners to implement programs that support the sending institution’s academic goals, align to best practices in the field, and fit within student and institutional budgets. The Custom Program Managers also plays a critical role on the CEA CAPA team in serving our partners and providing responsive, creative solutions. The incumbent must have a strong project management background, including attention to detail, critical and problem-solving skills, and willingness to learn and work within a small, fun, and dynamic team. This position involves collaboration and interactions with multiple internal and external stakeholders, so a successful candidate must be a strong communicator, both in writing and in-person interactions.

Responsibilities

The job duties listed below are not all inclusive of what the employee may be responsible for. Other duties may be assigned.

Provide direct support to U.S. faculty and administrators in partnership with CEA CAPA’s domestic and international team providing excellent customer service and problem-solving skills.
Manage a portfolio of 30+ custom programs per year.
Coordinate pre-departure program preparations between the sending U.S. institutional partner and CEA CAPA onsite staff, including leading planning calls, answering program and billing questions, and addressing any concerns that may arise.

Work in partnership with the Institutional Relations and Strategic Engagement Team, monitor partnering institutions enrollment numbers and provide feedback on where additional recruitment support and campus visits may be useful to reach and exceed targeted enrollment numbers per term.
Build and maintain program opportunities and offerings in our CRM system.
Support the institutional partners on any visa requirements and the visa application processes with guidance from our Visa Operations Team.
Advise CEA CAPA institutional partners on internship related eligibility requirements, questions, and concerns with guidance from our Career and Internship Team.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders to establish and maintain a pre-departure communication plan and timeline for participants (students and program leaders) on custom programs.
Manage relationships and communication with the study abroad administrators at partnering colleges and universities on topics including overseas crises, and student issues that arise while a student is on a CEA CAPA Custom Program in partnership with both the CEA CAPA onsite team and the Health, Safety, Student Advising Team.
Lead the RFP (request for proposal) process for all new and repeat custom programs.

Power confident decisions at Cars.com

Cars.com is the marketplace millions of people trust to buy and sell cars with confidence.

More than 25 years ago, we started as a simple idea, connect buyers and sellers, and today we do a lot more: trusted reviews, transparent pricing, and real-time, proprietary data that cut through the noise of one of life's biggest purchases. We win together or not at all. Here, your work counts, your ideas can help shape what’s next, and you’ll build alongside people who have your back.

We’re in the middle of a real transformation, modernizing the company and investing in AI and data to move faster. You're joining the No. 1 brand people think of first when shopping for a car, at the exact moment it's being rebuilt for what's next. You help decide what that becomes. That kind of influence is rare, and it's exactly why this is a place worth building your career.

Don't just take our word for it, we're proud to be named one of Built In's 2026 Best Places to Work in Chicago and across the U.S.

Ready to help build the most trusted place to buy and sell a car? Join us.

About The Position

Dealer Inspire / Cars.com is a certified provider of multiple products and services within many automotive Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) programs. These certifications allow for franchise dealer enrollments and significantly contribute to the market penetration of products and revenue generated for the company. The Senior OEM Program Manager will lead an OEM Program(s) to successfully manage business objectives, client relationships and work pipelines necessary to maintain and grow these OEM program affiliations.

This Senior OEM Program Manager will be well-versed in software technology and digital marketing and will excel in developing client relationships. This Senior OEM Program Manager will work in direct relationships with OEM clients to lead and manage the work request pipeline, facilitate business meetings, identify and consult to new opportunities, and troubleshoot/resolve issues. This Senior OEM Program Manager will be the business point of contact, partnering and interacting closely with the Technical Program Manager to serve each program’s technical needs. The Senior, OEM Program Manager will also coordinate and build strong relationships with internal Technology, Product, Operations, Marketing, and Sales departments for ensuring the successful implementation and high-quality delivery of all program strategy, growth, and technical opportunities and deliverables.

OEM program pipelines include both routine maintenance efforts as well as the introduction of more complex integrations and large-scale projects requiring Senior OEM Program Manager in full partnership with Technical Program Manager to help set expectations, evaluate priorities, understand desired outcomes and manage a project plan and roadmap to ensure smooth execution. The role of Senior OEM Program Manager will oversee these activities across multiple projects for the Program, in partnership with the Technical Program Manager, helping provide direction to team members and clients, helping resolve priority conflicts, and maintaining a rollup view and client roadmap of the overall work pipeline related to managing the program. Additionally, the Senior OEM Program Manager will operate in close partnership with leaders across Technology, Product, Operations, Marketing, and Sales departments to continuously communicate Program information and documentation, including strategic priorities, opportunities and timelines, in order to help identify needed resource allocation, and to provide analysis of program successes against business objectives.

The primary goals of the Senior OEM Program Manager role are to balance the strategic business opportunities and needs of the managed OEM program(s) against internal business goals and organizational priorities while developing and leading the client strategy and relationships. The ideal candidate is a proven leader with thorough experience building and maintaining high-efficiency workflows, successful client relationship development, and excellent communication channels for working with high-profile programs or client accounts.

Functions Of The Role

Lead and manage a portfolio of multiple medium sized or individual large-sized OEM programs, focusing on business growth, opportunity development, technology innovation, client and partner/agency relationship stability, and operational excellence across all products and services.
Consult, advise and recommend software, technical, digital strategies for clients through regular virtual and in-person engagements, meetings and communications, while staying knowledgeable on industry trends and all product offerings and services
Maintain close working partnerships with all external and internal leaders across functional areas and client/partner counterparts to drive continuous communication cadence of all program initiatives to maximize success
In partnership with Technical Program Manager, manage task intake from OEM clients including shared alignment on request triage, scope definition, outcomes, dev hour allotments or budget, and the setting of clear timeline and deliverable expectations.
In partnership with Technical Program Manager, responsible for communicating updates and maintaining accurate status assessments on project progress to OEM clients and internal business stakeholders.
Initiate and collaborate on goals for OEM programs aligned with business and technical objectives. Measure and communicate progress towards these goals.
Accountable for understanding health scores and satisfaction across all programs, identifying areas for improvement and resolving in collaboration with the technical teams.
Apply change, risk, and resource management to balance the needs of program(s) and evolve operations through partnership with internal departments..
Lead across program and projects to maintain strategy and process for continuous client and program performance improvements, including analysis and determination of actionable insights from aggregated program product performance data
Maintain a roadmap of program business strategy and client requested projects and objectives, partnering with leadership and Technical Program Manager to guide prioritization and resource distribution. Keep leadership informed through progress reports and risk/opportunity analysis.
Maintain program profitability (revenue vs. cost) and opportunity, providing regular updates and tracking.
Collaborate with leadership to create and refine strategic objectives within current and future programs.
Primary first point of contact responsibility for Program Brand and compliance requirements, technical integration and specifications requirements, contract terms, performance SLAs, product performance reporting deliverables, billing reconciliations and governance, and market share trending.

Required Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business management, digital marketing, computer sciences, software engineering, technology/project management, or similar practical experience.
3-5+ years of experience in program, product, or project management or similar roles.
Prior Business to Business Experience with OEMs or Large Dealer Groups
Record of successful, high value account/program management, preferably within the automotive industry.
Thorough knowledge and proficiency in program, product, project management, and SDLC methodologies.
Strong ability to balance stakeholders through negotiation and organizational savvy.
Experience managing people and leading through influence of others
Experiencing managing executive level or high value accounts with excellent presentation, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Excellent customer service skills and ability to understand client needs
Outstanding presentation, communication and delivery skills to engage clients and team members. Must possess the ability to present over the phone and in person
Fast learner with willingness to embrace the ever-changing software, technical, digital marketing landscape and strong problem-solving capability
Strong performance, with exceptional organizational and process skills, with the ability to execute a roadmap and plan.
Ability to understand technical tasks in a variety of software applications, tech stacks, and systems with experience collaborating with software development teams.
Understanding of product lifecycle development, Agile, and other SDLC methodologies.
Knowledge of all software, technical, digital products
Website infrastructure and technology
Analytics and Reporting (Google GA4)
SEO principles and fundamentals
Digital Advertising/Media

jobs.title: Project Manager, PV/BESS
jobs.description:
Clēnera is a tier-one developer and independent power producer located in Boise, Idaho, and is the U.S. subsidiary of Enlight Renewable Energy (Nasdaq: ENLT). We develop, finance, construct, own, and operate utility-scale solar and energy storage facilities throughout the United States. In its 2025 analysis of solar independent power producers, S&P Global ranked Clēnera as a top ten U.S. owner of planned installations in the next five years. Clēnera has over 1.9 GW of solar and 5.1 GWh of storage in operations or construction, and a development pipeline totaling 17.8 GW of solar and 51.1 GWh of storage across 23 states. Our company culture is at the core of everything we do, so you'll regularly find Caring, Committed, and Courageous individuals who value respectful, cross-functional collaboration with partners internally and externally. With our tremendous portfolio growth, we are increasing our headcount to meet the demands of the business. Are you ready to change the world with us?

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Project Manager independently leads 2-4 complex construction projects, setting the execution strategy, proactively managing schedule and budget risks, and driving cross-functional accountability to meet contractual and compliance requirements. You will serve as the primary owner representative for delivery performance, stakeholder alignment, change control, and successful commissioning and turnover.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own execution readiness by validating scope, drawings, specifications, contract requirements, and project controls are established, and ensuring project documentation standards are implemented and sustained in Procore.
Drive regulatory, permitting, and interconnection readiness by confirming permitting status, ensuring regulatory conditions are satisfied, and verifying utility interconnection agreements are in place and aligned with schedule needs.
Lead schedule development and control by building and maintaining an integrated schedule with EPC and Pre‑Construction partners, identifying critical path threats early, and initiating recovery actions as soon as slippage is identified.
Direct procurement and logistics coordination by validating procurement plans for major materials/equipment, aligning delivery timing with construction sequencing, and actively managing delivery and inventory risks that could affect progress.
Establish project-wide safety expectations by implementing safety protocols and training plans with the EPC, monitoring compliance, and ensuring corrective actions are executed promptly when risks are identified.
Lead project kickoff and major activity kickoffs by aligning internal teams, EPC partners, and key stakeholders on strategy, milestones, roles, and project controls for consistent execution.
Manage project financial performance by owning CAPEX/EPC budget tracking, spend curve management, cost code governance, and rigorous review of EPC billing, invoices, and supporting documentation to support accurate payment recommendations.
Execute disciplined change management by evaluating change drivers, verifying documentation, assessing schedule/cost impacts, and ensuring change orders are integrated into project baselines and payment processes.
Coordinate quality and inspection interfaces by planning and supporting AHJ and Independent Engineer (IE) inspections, tracking outcomes, and ensuring quality assurance actions remain aligned to contract deliverables and schedule needs.
Lead commissioning, closeout, and turnover by managing punch list completion, verifying as-builts and O&M documentation, coordinating training for operations/maintenance personnel, closing contracts/final payments, and capturing lessons learned.
Collaborate with individual department, as well as cross-functionally with other departments within the organization.
Maintain organizational excellence in terms of project timelines and deliverables.
Demonstrates the Clēnera Core Values of Caring, Committed, and Courageous.
Other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Education: Bachelor's degree in construction management, engineering, business, or related field experience.
Experience:
Minimum of 5 years of experience in construction project management, and;
Minimum of 2 years of experience executing utility-scale renewable energy projects.

Technology: Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Procore, and an ability to learn company-specific software programs, tools, processes, and machines.
Skills/Attributes:
Advanced mastery of schedule and cost controls, including critical path analysis, recovery planning, earned value, EAC forecasting, and cash flow management.
Strong EPC contract administration and negotiation skills, capable of structuring clear change orders, resolving claims, and driving accountability to contractual obligations.
Technical fluency in utility‑scale solar and energy storage construction.
Risk leadership, adept at identifying systemic and emergent risks, quantifying impacts, and implementing mitigation actions that protect COD and budget objectives.
Stakeholder management excellence, able to build trust and effectively coordinate with utilities, AHJs, inspectors, lenders' engineers, and EPC executives to clear critical path issues.
Quality and safety stewardship, ensuring QA/QC programs, inspection/test plans, NCR management, and HSSE requirements are embedded in the execution plan and measured against KPIs.
Clear, persuasive communication, producing concise, decision‑ready reporting for senior leadership and guiding the project team toward shared outcomes.
Team leadership and mentorship, setting expectations, delegating workstreams, coaching PM I/APMs, and reinforcing disciplined project management practices.
Self-motivated to work through complex problems and competing priorities, including a high level of detail and organization.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Money as a Service (MaaS) oversees a diverse portfolio of Stripe's core products and platforms, and our vision is to become the financial operating system for platforms and marketplaces globally.. These offerings facilitate the global movement and management of funds for users. The teams that fall under the MaaS umbrella are Connect, Money Management, and Crypto. Together, these teams work to ensure Stripe users have the robust financial infrastructure and tools they need to power their businesses on a global scale.

What you’ll do

As a TPM, you will play a key role leading complex programs across multiple engineering, product and cross-functional (finance, legal, compliance, risk, and other) teams spanning Stripe. You will be responsible for the successful definition, cross-functional strategy, planning and execution of large-scale technical programs that help to solve complex problems and empower Stripe and our users.

Drive functional and technical delivery of key team and org-wide programs/initiatives.
Partner with Engineering Managers, Product Managers and other cross functional partners to define, scope, and drive large programs to conclusion.
Develop, implement, and iterate on program management techniques, frameworks, and KPIs to achieve goals with well defined success criteria.
Make substantial improvements to how the teams you work with communicate and operate to significantly increase the productivity and efficiency of the teams.
Define and produce high quality written proposals, communications and documentation.
Leverage data and acquired knowledge to drive strategic decisions at an engineering leadership level.
Create widely circulated plans, driving consistency, clarity and building alignment across teams.
Help influence peers / leaders and build consensus while dealing with ambiguity.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

6+ years of software engineering, systems engineering and/or technical program management experience.
Excellent analytical skills; you digest complex information and make recommendations.
You have a track record of providing program management during all phases of software development from kick-off to launch, demonstrating critical thinking, challenging the norms and thought leadership.
You have very strong written and verbal communication skills, building strong relationships with stakeholders, teams and senior leaders around the organization.
You can drive internal and external process improvements across multiple teams and functions and bring a wealth of experience, opinions, proposals and best practices.
Experience operating autonomously and leading large-scale efforts across multiple teams and functions, with stakeholders in different disciplines across time zones.
Ability to understand how functionality comes together (across products and platforms) to deliver value for users, and identify/mitigate delivery risks proactively; can propose and drive a technical solution
Users-first and customer-focused mindset

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience in a global FinTech or banking organization

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Stripes on the Works in Progress team based in the London, UK office also work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual salary range for this role in the primary location is RON 244,800 - RON 367,200. This range may change if you are hired in another location. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings (“OTE”) range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and specific location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the primary location may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Specific benefits and details about what compensation is included in the salary range listed above will vary depending on the applicant’s location and can be discussed in more detail during the interview process. Benefits/additional compensation for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; retirement plans; health benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Regulatory Reporting
jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The Software Quality Operations (SWQOps) team is at the heart of ensuring the safety, reliability, and quality of the Waymo Driver. Our mission is to build an adaptable and scalable operation, increasingly powered by AI, to deliver the crucial insights necessary to confidently deploy and grow Waymo's autonomous vehicle service.

Why This Team Is Essential To Waymo's Success

Waymo is undergoing unprecedented growth, rapidly expanding into new cities (targeting ~20 new cities by EOY 2026) and launching new vehicle platforms. SWQ Ops plays a critical role in this expansion, making it possible to scale safely and efficiently. The Regulatory Reporting Operations team within SWQ Ops owns the scaled delivery of datasets and methodologies used to evaluate events of regulatory interest and ensure reporting accuracy as Waymo continues to scale. We are on the front lines of:

De-risking New Deployments: Through meticulous triage of driving and simulated events, issue discovery, and continuous field monitoring, SWQ Ops provides early warnings and critical insights. This "early intervention in RO issue detection" ensures operational resilience and safety, particularly in new and complex environments, which is critical as Waymo enters multiple new cities and ramps up platforms like Ojai.
Enabling International RO & Market Expansion: Our team is deeply integrated into every stage of Waymo's market entry framework, from initial city evaluation (OK2Plan) to scaling operations (OK2Scale). We provide the necessary data analysis, policy development, and quality assurance to unblock critical milestones, preventing slowdowns in market expansion velocity.
Data Flywheel: Supporting the development of a single, automated, end-to-end machine learning flywheel for the entire Waymo Driver. A successful flywheel will be the core engine for scaling our technology, enabling faster international expansion, quicker remediation of driving issues, and a significant reduction in the engineering effort required to maintain and improve the driver.
Driving Engineering Velocity: By handling the vital work of performance evaluation, issue deep-dives, and data set curation, SWQOps collaborates heavily and allows Waymo's Engineering, SysEng, Simulation, and Data Science teams to focus on their core tasks of developing and improving the Waymo Driver.
Workflow Incubation & Development: Incubating high-impact workflows and ensuring readiness for automation and long-term operational excellence.

You Will

Drive outcomes for large and complex technical operations programs that span multiple organizations. Develop and drive execution on strategic roadmaps, own forecasting and resource planning.
Partner with the Regulatory Compliance team to operationalize reporting requirements and be responsible for standing up new workflows and scaling existing workflows to support US and International expansions.
Define program / workflow KPIs and SLAs. Drive high-quality outcomes through deployments with a global vendor workforce.
Drive workflow transformation efforts to meet evolving business needs. Partner with Engineering to design, test, and deploy cutting-edge Machine Learning (ML) and Generative AI (Gen-AI) models and tools to drive step-change improvements in issue discovery & detection, triage efficiency, and quality assurance.
Communicate overall program status, risks and current priorities to executive stakeholders. Drive strategic decisions making across functions.
Mentor a high-performing team of Technical Specialists, fostering a culture of "quality-first" in a high-velocity environment.

You Have

Bachelor's degree in technical, legal or business discipline
10+ years of experience managing complex, tech-enabled operations and experience working across cross-functional partners (Legal, Product, Engineering, Data Science, Systems Engineering) to drive outcomes
5+ years of people management experience
Experience in Regulatory Compliance, Vehicle Qualification, or similar domains, and ability to assess and operationalize legal reporting requirements
Proven ability to manage complex technical operations programs, including structuring project plans, identifying dependencies, and driving execution
Ability to thrive in a high ambiguity, dynamic environment

We Prefer

Experience working with offshore teams / multiple local operations hubs
Experience within A / V space
Increased competency in supporting all phases of the machine learning development lifecycle, from data preparation and training to validation, deployment, and continuous monitoring
Experience with Lean / Six Sigma process improvement methodologies

Benefits

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Octant is a clinical-stage drug discovery company developing correctors for protein misfolding diseases. We are a well-backed team of experienced scientists and entrepreneurs at the frontiers of biology, chemistry, and computation, combining high-throughput synthetic biology, generative chemistry, and AI/ML to repeatedly develop precision medicines for genetically defined diseases.

JOB DESCRIPTION
We are looking for an experienced program manager to keep Octant's first program in the clinic moving on time and on budget. OCT-980, our first-in-human oral corrector for RHO-associated autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa, is currently in a Phase 1/2 trial. As program manager, you will own the integrated plan across all functional workstreams, keep the team aligned on timelines, budget, risks, and decisions and ensure program activities are coordinated and communicated to stakeholders.
Octant takes a novel, technology-forward approach to drug development, so there isn’t a standard playbook to follow. This role offers the opportunity to bring structure and rigor to a fast-moving team that's charting its own course. The program manager will report to the Chief Medical Officer.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Develop and maintain the integrated program plan, partnering with Development Team stakeholders to pressure-test and optimize the program execution timeline Clinical Development (including enrollment, site activation, database lock, and the final study report) and aligning it with CMC, drug supply, nonclinical, regulatory, and finance workstreams.
Identify critical path activities and cross-functional interdependencies, and work with workstream owners to resolve rate-limiting steps.
Develop and manage the program budget in partnership with Finance, anticipating changes in cost or timing.
Support the management of program resources including CROs, vendors, and consultants, tracking deliverables, milestones, and spend against contracts and budget.
Gather cross-functional input from clinical development, drug supply, nonclinical, and other functions to support leadership decision-making.
Maintain program risk and decision logs, with clear mitigation plans and escalation as needed.
Plan, facilitate, and document core and program team meetings, and communicate program status, milestones, and risks to senior leadership.
Work effectively across a matrixed team, influencing without direct authority and gathering information from stakeholders proactively.

THIS JOB MIGHT BE GREAT FOR YOU IF YOU HAVE:
Ideally 10 years of project or program management experience in life sciences; minimum of 5 years. Experience across the clinical development stages is a plus.
Experience on complex therapeutic programs (e.g., immunology, oncology) is preferred; ophthalmology experience is ideal.
A track record of building and maintaining integrated plans across functions, and of delivering programs on time and within budget.
Experience tracking program budgets, partnering with Finance, and managing contracts and vendors such as CROs.
The ability to work effectively across scientific, clinical, technical, and financial domains, and to communicate clearly, proactively, and collaboratively with stakeholders at every level.
Comfort with changing priorities, and the ability to anticipate issues and help the team make decisions before they become critical.
A Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline or a related field; an advanced degree is a plus. Equivalent experience can substitute for formal degree programs.
PMP or program management training is a plus; strong analytical, conflict-resolution, and communication skills are essential.

The expected annual salary for this role is in the range of $150,000 to $185,000, depending on experience level. We offer health benefits (medical, dental, vision), equity, and 401(k) matching.

Octant is located in Emeryville, California and our team works onsite.

Octant is an equal opportunity company that values applicants of all backgrounds. We're committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive work environment. We value less traditional backgrounds, and may consider an equivalent combination of knowledge, skills, education, and experience to meet minimum qualifications. We know that confidence-gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting spectacular candidates, so please don't hesitate to apply — we'd love to hear from you.

Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

The Program Management Office (PMO) is how Lambda turns strategy into delivered results. As a Technical Program Manager, you will drive complex, cross-functional programs that span our AI infrastructure, hardware, data center, and product organizations. You will bring structure to ambiguity, keep programs on schedule, and make sure Engineering, Operations, Product, and customer-facing teams are aligned on what we’re building, how we’re testing it, and when it ships.

What You’ll Do

Lead multiple concurrent, large-scale programs, such as GPU cluster deployments in colocation data centers across the country, from planning through delivery
Define program scope, milestones, and success metrics, and keep them current as priorities shift
Proactively identify risks and dependencies, anticipate execution issues, and drive them to resolution

Communicate progress, risks, and decisions clearly to executives, internal teams, and customers across locations and time zones
Work with internal and external stakeholders at all levels to resolve technical and scheduling issues
Build strong partnerships across Lambda, using your credibility and technical acumen to drive process improvements and operating efficiencies
Contribute to PMO standards, tooling, and best practices, and help scale how Lambda plans and executes
Contribute to the development of new business opportunities and the expansion of existing ones

You

5+ years of program or project management experience on complex technical or product development programs
A thorough understanding of both agile and waterfall methodologies, and the judgment to know when to apply each
A technical background, typically an engineering degree or equivalent hands-on experience, with the ability to engage credibly on technical topics
Excellent leadership and organizational skills
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to structure messaging for internal and external audiences
The ability to lead humbly, by influence and by example
Proficiency with project and program management tools [e.g., Jira, Asana, Smartsheet, MS Project]
Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to create structure where none exists

Experience in the machine learning or computer hardware industry
Experience in a manufacturing environment with complex systems integration
Experience with large-scale, distributed data center environments
PMP, PgMP, or similar certification

Cretex Medical is a leading contract manufacturer of precision components and assemblies for the medical device industry. Our customers view us as a trusted partner in the areas of injection molding, laser processing, metal stamping and device assembly. Learn more at www.cretexmedical.com .

P Osition Summary

The Program Manager will support the Laser Processing business unit, and will be responsible for facilitating all aspects of the engineering projects for assigned customers from the early prototyping stage all the way into a production program. This position acts as the customer advocate and leads customer programs that ensures compliance to customer, industry, and company requirements and standards. This position may supervise employees.

Program Manager Responsibilities:

Administer and manage customer projects through the new product engineering stage gate process to meet requirements, scope, schedule, budget, and quality expectations
Ensure compliance to the company Quality Management System (QMS), policies and procedures, regulatory agency standards and guidelines, and customer specifications throughout the development cycle
Build and maintain a positive working relationship with internal and external customers
Direct and assume responsibility for the actions and performance of the NPI cross-functional team. Facilitate teamwork between departments
Create project plans/timelines and promote a sense of urgency to ensure successful commercial launch
Understand manufacturing capabilities and capacity of the organization
Understand manufacturing and engineering processes that relate to the medical device industry
Support estimating efforts for company products and services
Lead discussions with customers and internal teams on designs, troubleshooting and finding cost-effective solutions
Manage/facilitate transfers to production
Communicate with customers on a routine basis and provides project plans, timelines, and milestones
Proactively recommends, promotes, and supports actions for implementing continuous improvement projects. Assists internal teams with cost reductions, root cause analysis, and corrective actions
Work closely with Engineering, Operations/Production, Supply Chain, Scheduling, and Quality to meet or beat customer delivery dates and On-Time-Delivery (OTD) performance
Work with Quality to facilitate customer required audits
Supports S&OP planning for assigned programs and customers

Qualifications

Program Manager Requirements:

Associates Degree in related field
4 years of experience in contract manufacturing and/or engineering role
Extensive experience with medical device contract manufacturing
Experience managing numerous projects simultaneously using appropriate software tools (i.e. Excel or Microsoft Project) and professionally communicating project status to customers
Understanding of Laser Processing and Assembly

Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering
PMP Certification

What is it like to work at Cretex Medical?

jobs.title: Staff Program Manager – Global Logistics & Trade Technology
jobs.description:
Requirements

Description & Requirements

who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About This Team

The Global Supply Chain Portfolio team supports portfolio management, transformation, and operations for Upstream Supply Chain and Global Fulfillment Technology. The organization is responsible for over $70M in capital delivery across more than 400 people.

This role leads global logistics and trade technology programs within that portfolio — spanning transportation, distribution, customs, and trade compliance — working across internal teams, third-party logistics providers, and vendor platforms.

The team is also evolving to take on a large portfolio transformation: elevating people, process, and technology through consistent delivery frameworks, capacity planning, budget management, dependency management, and portfolio reporting. The goal is to simplify and enable managers and directors in Global Supply Chain Technology, giving them more time and better insight to elevate their programs and portfolios.

Core Responsibilities

As a Staff Program Manager, you will lead complex technology programs across multiple teams and organizational boundaries, establishing program approaches and delivery practices that drive measurable business value. You will manage program complexity, dependencies, and risks, ensure alignment with organizational priorities, and drive informed program decisions. You will partner with senior stakeholders, define delivery standards and governance, mentor program managers, and influence organizational delivery practices to improve execution, predictability, and outcomes across portfolios.

Select Responsibilities Include

Lead complex technology programs across global logistics and trade domains — transportation, distribution, customs, and trade compliance — coordinating delivery across multiple teams and external partners
Engage with technology leadership and senior stakeholders driving program decisions and coordinating cross-organization initiatives
Define program approach for technology initiatives establishing clear direction and multi-quarter delivery planning
Drive technology program delivery success using Agile methodologies, coordinating teams and managing dependencies across logistics, trade, and fulfillment technology domains
Manage program delivery against externally set regulatory and trade compliance deadlines, where dates are fixed and non-delivery carries financial or operational consequence
Coordinate delivery across third-party dependencies — logistics providers, carriers, brokers, and vendor platforms — where program timelines depend on partners outside direct organizational control
Plan and sequence program delivery around operational constraints including peak season change freezes, site readiness, and cutover windows that limit when technology changes can land
Establish program quality standards through governance approaches, risk management, and delivery readiness for programs that affect live distribution and fulfillment operations
Analyze technology landscape identifying opportunities for program improvements and delivery optimization
Contribute to portfolio-level practices including capacity planning, financial management, and dependency reporting across Global Supply Chain Technology
Mentor program managers on complex coordination challenges including cross-team dependencies and stakeholder management

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, or equivalent experience; Master’s degree or PMP preferred
9-12 years of program management, project management, technology program coordination, or business analysis experience, or equivalent
Proven experience leading planning and execution across a portfolio of programs within a domain; track record of aligning delivery to strategic priorities and managing interdependencies
Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders to align portfolio priorities, investments, and delivery outcomes; experience resolving stakeholder conflicts and trade-offs
Experience overseeing portfolio-level dependencies and risks; familiarity with establishing domain-level risk and dependency management frameworks
Proven track record of coordinating portfolio delivery across programs to optimize execution and resource alignment
Experience establishing Agile delivery standards for programs; familiarity with coaching program managers on scaling Agile practices to organizational context
Experience delivering technology programs in logistics, transportation, distribution, or global trade domains; familiarity with platforms such as TMS, WMS, or global trade management systems and carrier, broker, or partner integrations
Experience leading programs involving third-party logistics providers or multi-site operational cutover, including delivery against regulatory or compliance-driven deadlines

must haves

Acknowledge the presence of choice in every moment and take personal responsibility for your life.
Possess an entrepreneurial spirit and continuously innovate to achieve great results.
Communicate with honesty and kindness and create the space for others to do the same.
Lead with courage, knowing the possibility of greatness is bigger than the fear of failure.
Foster connection by putting people first and building trusting relationships.
Integrate fun and joy as a way of being and working, aka doesn’t take yourself too seriously.

Additional Notes

Authorization to work in Canada is required for this role.

Compensation And Benefits Package

lululemon’s compensation offerings are grounded in a pay-for-performance philosophy that recognizes exceptional individual and team performance. The typical hiring range for this position is from  $ 160,100 - $210,100 annually
; the base pay offered is based on market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards offering, permanent employees in this position may be eligible for our competitive annual bonus program, subject to program eligibility requirements.  

At Lululemon, Investing In Our People Is a Top Priority. We Believe That When Life Works, Work Works. We Strive To Be The Place Where Inclusive Leaders Come To Develop And Enable All To Be Well. jobs.description:
Calling all innovators - find your future at Fiserv.

We're Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants and consumers to one another millions of times a day - quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we're involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.

Job Title

Senior Technical Project Manager

About Your Role

You will lead complex technical projects that support product delivery, platform readiness, and business outcomes across Fiserv. You will work with technology engineering, products, operations, risk, and business stakeholders to define plans, manage dependencies, and drive execution. This role matters because it improves delivery predictability, aligns cross-functional work, and supports scalable, reliable solutions.

What You'll Do

Lead cross-functional technical programs from intake through delivery, aligning scope, milestones, dependencies, and success measures.
Develop integrated program plans, track progress against commitments, and drive issue resolution across engineering, infrastructure, product, and business teams.
Evaluate program risks, document mitigation plans, and escalate decisions with clear impact, tradeoff, and timing considerations.
Facilitate planning, status reviews, and stakeholder communications using consistent reporting, meeting cadences, and action tracking.
Partner with technical teams to translate business objectives into executable workstreams, delivery sequencing, and release readiness activities.
Develop program governance artifacts, including roadmaps, dependency maps, decision logs, and executive-ready updates.
Improve delivery execution by identifying process gaps, standardizing workflows, and measuring outcomes across multiple initiatives.
Responsibilities listed are not intended to be all-inclusive and may be modified as necessary.

Experience You'll Need To Have

6+ years of experience in technical program management, technical product delivery, or project leadership within software, platform, or enterprise technology environments.
6+ years of experience leading large, complex, cross-functional initiatives with engineering, infrastructure, product management, operations, and business stakeholders.
6+ years of experience using structured delivery methods such as Agile, Scrum, Kanban, Waterfall, or hybrid program frameworks.
Experience using program and project tools to manage roadmaps, risks, dependencies, status reporting, and delivery milestones.
Experience communicating technical concepts, delivery tradeoffs, and program status to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Bachelor’s degree in business, computer science, engineering, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education, related experience and/or military experience.

Experience That Would Be Great To Have

Experience in financial services, payments, fintech, or regulated technology environments.
Experience supporting enterprise platform programs, application modernization, or systems integration efforts.

gTech's Extended Workforce Solutions (xWS) team empowers Product Areas (PAs) to optimize outsourced operations while reducing risks and driving efficiency through the enforcement of Google best practices and policies. Role Description

Cyber Recovery Project Manager Sr. – Exercises

The Role

Lead the planning, execution, and continuous improvement of enterprise Cyber Recovery exercises, ensuring critical infrastructure, applications, dependencies, recovery playbooks, and decision-making processes are validated against realistic cyber-disruption scenarios. This supports the current Cyber Recovery operating model, which includes exercise execution and resolution of issues identified through exercises.

What You’ll Do

Exercise Program Management: Own the end-to-end exercise lifecycle, including scope, objectives, scenarios, schedules, participants, dependencies, execution, and reporting.
Scenario & Exercise Planning: Coordinate realistic ransomware/destructive-event tabletop, simulation, and technical recovery exercises across infrastructure, cloud, security, and application teams.
Recovery Playbook Validation: Validate recovery playbooks for completeness, technical accuracy, usability, recovery sequencing, and actionable restoration steps.
Dependency & RTO/RPO Validation: Ensure exercises test critical dependencies such as DNS, DHCP, Identity, network, storage/backup, databases, cloud, and application services before broader restoration. These dependencies are specifically identified in the current Cyber Recovery assessment scope.
Cross-Functional Coordination: Drive participation across Cyber Recovery, Infrastructure, Public Cloud, Information Security, Application teams, Operations, Incident Response, business stakeholders, and vendors.
Exercise Execution & Facilitation: Manage exercise logistics, injects, decision points, technical recovery activities, escalations, and stakeholder communications.
After-Action Reviews: Produce exercise results, lessons learned, gaps, bottlenecks, and recommendations, leveraging findings across successive exercises to identify recurring weaknesses.
Remediation Tracking: Convert exercise findings into actionable remediation plans with owners, priorities, target dates, risks, and closure criteria.
Metrics & Reporting: Maintain exercise dashboards and KPIs covering readiness, participation, recovery performance, RTO/RPO attainment, findings, remediation aging, and overall program maturity.
Audit & Compliance Support: Maintain exercise evidence and documentation to demonstrate recovery readiness and support Internal Audit, regulatory, and risk-management requirements. The Cyber Recovery model specifically embeds audit readiness and remediation tracking into ongoing operations.
