new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager - Site Lead
new_jobs.description:
Perkins&Will Science & Technology

Our SF studio, 120+ people inside a 3,000-person global firm, is delivering a state-of-the-art science and technology campus, and we are seeking a Senior Project Manager to serve as site lead. This is the person who sees the whole project at once and keeps every team, consultant, and client stakeholder pointed in the same direction.

You'll be on site regularly, running the coordination that holds a multi-building campus together: a consultant team spanning landscape, site utilities, and field operations; a client with many voices; and a schedule where one building's delay ripples into the next. You need enough technical depth in complex projects to spot a problem early, ask the right questions, and bring in the right expert when appropriate.

What You'll Own

Serve as site lead and the senior on-site representative of the design team, with the authority to convene, coordinate, and escalate.
Oversee the full consultant team, including landscape, civil and site utilities, MEP, structural, process piping, and hold each to scope, schedule, and quality.
Keep all site utilities moving as one project. Manage the interfaces between site utilities, phases, and site infrastructure, so a decision in one place doesn't create a problem somewhere else.
Own the campus-level master schedule and phasing strategy. Work with Project Architects, engineers, client and general contractor representatives to head off schedule conflicts as the project changes.
Ensure documentation considers full coordination of all site utilities, infrastructure, and landscape with building systems, including utility routing, tie-ins, shutdowns, and the campus-wide services that labs depend on.
Facilitate and administer the permitting process for all site-related permits. Review submitted permit drawings and specifications, prepare validation reports summarizing findings, and administer the permit submission, plan-check response, and resubmission process by organizing comments and consolidating responses. Engineers of Record remain responsible for all technical responses, design, and documentation.
Track interfaces between site work and future building projects, including work performed under separate permits or contracts, so nothing falls between permit packages.

Lead senior client management: steering committees, executive updates, and the relationships that keep trust intact when things get hard.
Run the alignment rhythm: Chair the integrated team meetings, coordination reviews, minutes and memos, and decision tracking. You're accountable for timely, complete communication between the client, consultants, contractors, and project team.
Partner with applicable engineers, architects, landscape architects and the contractor on constructability, sequencing, site logistics, and safety, and oversee construction administration through closeout.
Manage risk at the program level. Monitor client and technical issues, surface them early to limit liability, frame options and consequences, and drive them to resolution.
Hold the quality bar high. Make sure documents are reviewed for accuracy, omissions, legibility, and compliance with the firm's Project Delivery Manual.
You will not be executing any documentation of drawings or specifications.

What You'll Bring

Experience:

10 to 15+ years in architecture or design and construction delivery, with significant time as a Senior Project Manager or Senior Project Architect on large, campus-scale or multi-building projects.
Site lead or field leadership experience on projects with multiple concurrent buildings or phases.
Technical depth in complex building facilities a plus: MEP-intensive systems, modular building systems, utility distribution, and specialized environments.
Working knowledge of site infrastructure, civil and utility coordination, and landscape integration.
Experience administering permit submissions and plan-check responses for site, civil, and utility work with local jurisdictions.
Fluency in building codes, life safety requirements, site analysis, specifications, contract documents, and construction contract administration, from project kickoff through closeout.
A track record of leading large consultant teams and holding them accountable.
Familiarity with collaborative delivery models (IPD, TVD, design-build, CM at Risk) is helpful. Deep TVD expertise is not required.

How you lead:

You see the whole board. You hold the big picture without losing track of what's at risk this week.
Calm, credible, and direct with the team, clients, contractors, and consultants.
You build alignment rather than mandate it, and you know when to make the call yourself.
Polished in executive and large stakeholder forums.
You build systems that let others run the details, so you can stay focused on what only you can see.

Software:

Microsoft Project or Smartsheet for master scheduling
Bluebeam Revu
Working knowledge of Revit and BIM coordination tools such as Navisworks or Autodesk Construction Cloud
Procore, Newforma, or similar construction management platforms a plus
Microsoft 365

Credentials:

Bachelor's degree in architecture or a related discipline, required
Architectural license required (or 20 years of project management and design experience)
PMP or equivalent a plus
LEED GA within 6 months of hire

What You'll Get

Salary range: $141,100-$207,300 commensurate with experience, education and skillset.

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) retirement plan and paid time off
Professional development stipend and dedicated continuing education time
Performance-based bonuses
Access to firmwide affinity groups and leadership development programs
Studio initiatives and events; a team that actually likes each other

AESC is an exciting, newly created global organization committed to solving the challenges of a sustainable future and becoming the leading supplier of full-value-chain battery solutions. AESC is headquartered in Japan and has battery manufacturing locations in Japan, UK, China, and the U.S.

AESC Mission

Our mission is to solve the challenges for a sustainable future. Together, we can make a meaningful impact.

We are seeking a detail-oriented and highly organized Project Manager to support the execution of utility-scale energy storage and infrastructure projects. This role will focus on project administration, scheduling, documentation, and internal cross-team coordination to ensure smooth delivery of complex projects. The Project Manager will work closely with sales managers, engineering teams, and external stakeholders to maintain project momentum from initiation through completion.

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Project Management, or related field (or equivalent experience).

Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Proficiency with project management tools (MS Project, Smartsheet, Asana, Jira) and Microsoft Office.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey technical and commercial information clearly.
Self-driven, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment

Knowledge of energy storage systems, renewable energy, or large-scale infrastructure projects.
Understanding of permitting, interconnection, and regulatory processes.
Experience supporting EPCs, utilities, IPPs, or project developers.
Familiarity with CRM platforms and project tracking systems.

Welcome to AESC, supporting our state-of-the-art Gigafactories, where you'll have the opportunity to tackle the world's most fascinating challenges alongside exceptionally talented individuals who are driven to make a difference. At AESC, we offer a comprehensive compensation package. In addition, we provide a range of valuable benefits, such as 401K, and health insurance. Highly automated, clean, safe, and temperature-controlled production environment

Career growth opportunities within project management, operations, or commercial functions.
Comprehensive benefits package including [health insurance, retirement plan, PTO, etc.].

Following the submission of your application, we are committed to providing timely responses to all applicants, though response times may vary depending on the volume of submissions. Power confident decisions at Cars.com

Cars.com is the marketplace millions of people trust to buy and sell cars with confidence.

More than 25 years ago, we started as a simple idea, connect buyers and sellers, and today we do a lot more: trusted reviews, transparent pricing, and real-time, proprietary data that cut through the noise of one of life's biggest purchases. At Cars.com, we debate openly, decide fast, and deliver what we say we will. We solve real problems for car shoppers and dealers, simplify for speed, and focus on what matters most. We win together or not at all. Here, your work counts, your ideas can help shape what’s next, and you’ll build alongside people who have your back.

We’re in the middle of a real transformation, modernizing the company and investing in AI and data to move faster. You're joining the No. 1 brand people think of first when shopping for a car, at the exact moment it's being rebuilt for what's next. You help decide what that becomes. That kind of influence is rare, and it's exactly why this is a place worth building your career.

Don't just take our word for it, we're proud to be named one of Built In's 2026 Best Places to Work in Chicago and across the U.S.

Ready to help build the most trusted place to buy and sell a car? Join us.

About The Position

Dealer Inspire / Cars.com is a certified provider of multiple products and services within many automotive Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) programs. These certifications allow for franchise dealer enrollments and significantly contribute to the market penetration of products and revenue generated for the company. The Senior OEM Program Manager will lead an OEM Program(s) to successfully manage business objectives, client relationships and work pipelines necessary to maintain and grow these OEM program affiliations.

This Senior OEM Program Manager will be well-versed in software technology and digital marketing and will excel in developing client relationships. This Senior OEM Program Manager will work in direct relationships with OEM clients to lead and manage the work request pipeline, facilitate business meetings, identify and consult to new opportunities, and troubleshoot/resolve issues. This Senior OEM Program Manager will be the business point of contact, partnering and interacting closely with the Technical Program Manager to serve each program’s technical needs. The Senior, OEM Program Manager will also coordinate and build strong relationships with internal Technology, Product, Operations, Marketing, and Sales departments for ensuring the successful implementation and high-quality delivery of all program strategy, growth, and technical opportunities and deliverables.

OEM program pipelines include both routine maintenance efforts as well as the introduction of more complex integrations and large-scale projects requiring Senior OEM Program Manager in full partnership with Technical Program Manager to help set expectations, evaluate priorities, understand desired outcomes and manage a project plan and roadmap to ensure smooth execution. The role of Senior OEM Program Manager will oversee these activities across multiple projects for the Program, in partnership with the Technical Program Manager, helping provide direction to team members and clients, helping resolve priority conflicts, and maintaining a rollup view and client roadmap of the overall work pipeline related to managing the program. Additionally, the Senior OEM Program Manager will operate in close partnership with leaders across Technology, Product, Operations, Marketing, and Sales departments to continuously communicate Program information and documentation, including strategic priorities, opportunities and timelines, in order to help identify needed resource allocation, and to provide analysis of program successes against business objectives.

The primary goals of the Senior OEM Program Manager role are to balance the strategic business opportunities and needs of the managed OEM program(s) against internal business goals and organizational priorities while developing and leading the client strategy and relationships. The ideal candidate is a proven leader with thorough experience building and maintaining high-efficiency workflows, successful client relationship development, and excellent communication channels for working with high-profile programs or client accounts.

Functions Of The Role

Lead and manage a portfolio of multiple medium sized or individual large-sized OEM programs, focusing on business growth, opportunity development, technology innovation, client and partner/agency relationship stability, and operational excellence across all products and services.
Consult, advise and recommend software, technical, digital strategies for clients through regular virtual and in-person engagements, meetings and communications, while staying knowledgeable on industry trends and all product offerings and services
Maintain close working partnerships with all external and internal leaders across functional areas and client/partner counterparts to drive continuous communication cadence of all program initiatives to maximize success
In partnership with Technical Program Manager, manage task intake from OEM clients including shared alignment on request triage, scope definition, outcomes, dev hour allotments or budget, and the setting of clear timeline and deliverable expectations.
In partnership with Technical Program Manager, responsible for communicating updates and maintaining accurate status assessments on project progress to OEM clients and internal business stakeholders.
Initiate and collaborate on goals for OEM programs aligned with business and technical objectives. Measure and communicate progress towards these goals.
Accountable for understanding health scores and satisfaction across all programs, identifying areas for improvement and resolving in collaboration with the technical teams.
Apply change, risk, and resource management to balance the needs of program(s) and evolve operations through partnership with internal departments..
Lead across program and projects to maintain strategy and process for continuous client and program performance improvements, including analysis and determination of actionable insights from aggregated program product performance data
Maintain a roadmap of program business strategy and client requested projects and objectives, partnering with leadership and Technical Program Manager to guide prioritization and resource distribution. Keep leadership informed through progress reports and risk/opportunity analysis.
Maintain program profitability (revenue vs. cost) and opportunity, providing regular updates and tracking.
Collaborate with leadership to create and refine strategic objectives within current and future programs.
Primary first point of contact responsibility for Program Brand and compliance requirements, technical integration and specifications requirements, contract terms, performance SLAs, product performance reporting deliverables, billing reconciliations and governance, and market share trending.

Required Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business management, digital marketing, computer sciences, software engineering, technology/project management, or similar practical experience.
3-5+ years of experience in program, product, or project management or similar roles.
Prior Business to Business Experience with OEMs or Large Dealer Groups
Record of successful, high value account/program management, preferably within the automotive industry.
Thorough knowledge and proficiency in program, product, project management, and SDLC methodologies.
Strong ability to balance stakeholders through negotiation and organizational savvy.
Experience managing people and leading through influence of others
Experiencing managing executive level or high value accounts with excellent presentation, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Excellent customer service skills and ability to understand client needs
Outstanding presentation, communication and delivery skills to engage clients and team members. Must possess the ability to present over the phone and in person
Fast learner with willingness to embrace the ever-changing software, technical, digital marketing landscape and strong problem-solving capability
Strong performance, with exceptional organizational and process skills, with the ability to execute a roadmap and plan.
Ability to understand technical tasks in a variety of software applications, tech stacks, and systems with experience collaborating with software development teams.
Understanding of product lifecycle development, Agile, and other SDLC methodologies.
Knowledge of all software, technical, digital products
Website infrastructure and technology
Analytics and Reporting (Google GA4)
SEO principles and fundamentals
Digital Advertising/Media
Required Certifications:
Google Analytics/Ads

new_jobs.description:
Clēnera is a tier-one developer and independent power producer located in Boise, Idaho, and is the U.S. subsidiary of Enlight Renewable Energy (Nasdaq: ENLT). We develop, finance, construct, own, and operate utility-scale solar and energy storage facilities throughout the United States. In its 2025 analysis of solar independent power producers, S&P Global ranked Clēnera as a top ten U.S. owner of planned installations in the next five years. Clēnera has over 1.9 GW of solar and 5.1 GWh of storage in operations or construction, and a development pipeline totaling 17.8 GW of solar and 51.1 GWh of storage across 23 states. Our company culture is at the core of everything we do, so you'll regularly find Caring, Committed, and Courageous individuals who value respectful, cross-functional collaboration with partners internally and externally. With our tremendous portfolio growth, we are increasing our headcount to meet the demands of the business. Are you ready to change the world with us?

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Project Manager independently leads 2-4 complex construction projects, setting the execution strategy, proactively managing schedule and budget risks, and driving cross-functional accountability to meet contractual and compliance requirements. You will serve as the primary owner representative for delivery performance, stakeholder alignment, change control, and successful commissioning and turnover.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own execution readiness by validating scope, drawings, specifications, contract requirements, and project controls are established, and ensuring project documentation standards are implemented and sustained in Procore.
Drive regulatory, permitting, and interconnection readiness by confirming permitting status, ensuring regulatory conditions are satisfied, and verifying utility interconnection agreements are in place and aligned with schedule needs.
Lead schedule development and control by building and maintaining an integrated schedule with EPC and Pre‑Construction partners, identifying critical path threats early, and initiating recovery actions as soon as slippage is identified.
Direct procurement and logistics coordination by validating procurement plans for major materials/equipment, aligning delivery timing with construction sequencing, and actively managing delivery and inventory risks that could affect progress.
Establish project-wide safety expectations by implementing safety protocols and training plans with the EPC, monitoring compliance, and ensuring corrective actions are executed promptly when risks are identified.
Lead project kickoff and major activity kickoffs by aligning internal teams, EPC partners, and key stakeholders on strategy, milestones, roles, and project controls for consistent execution.
Manage project financial performance by owning CAPEX/EPC budget tracking, spend curve management, cost code governance, and rigorous review of EPC billing, invoices, and supporting documentation to support accurate payment recommendations.
Execute disciplined change management by evaluating change drivers, verifying documentation, assessing schedule/cost impacts, and ensuring change orders are integrated into project baselines and payment processes.
Coordinate quality and inspection interfaces by planning and supporting AHJ and Independent Engineer (IE) inspections, tracking outcomes, and ensuring quality assurance actions remain aligned to contract deliverables and schedule needs.
Lead commissioning, closeout, and turnover by managing punch list completion, verifying as-builts and O&M documentation, coordinating training for operations/maintenance personnel, closing contracts/final payments, and capturing lessons learned.
Collaborate with individual department, as well as cross-functionally with other departments within the organization.
Maintain organizational excellence in terms of project timelines and deliverables.
Demonstrates the Clēnera Core Values of Caring, Committed, and Courageous.
Other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Education: Bachelor's degree in construction management, engineering, business, or related field experience.
Experience:
Minimum of 5 years of experience in construction project management, and;
Minimum of 2 years of experience executing utility-scale renewable energy projects.

Technology: Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Procore, and an ability to learn company-specific software programs, tools, processes, and machines.
Skills/Attributes:
Advanced mastery of schedule and cost controls, including critical path analysis, recovery planning, earned value, EAC forecasting, and cash flow management.
Strong EPC contract administration and negotiation skills, capable of structuring clear change orders, resolving claims, and driving accountability to contractual obligations.
Technical fluency in utility‑scale solar and energy storage construction.
Risk leadership, adept at identifying systemic and emergent risks, quantifying impacts, and implementing mitigation actions that protect COD and budget objectives.
Stakeholder management excellence, able to build trust and effectively coordinate with utilities, AHJs, inspectors, lenders' engineers, and EPC executives to clear critical path issues.
Quality and safety stewardship, ensuring QA/QC programs, inspection/test plans, NCR management, and HSSE requirements are embedded in the execution plan and measured against KPIs.
Clear, persuasive communication, producing concise, decision‑ready reporting for senior leadership and guiding the project team toward shared outcomes.
Team leadership and mentorship, setting expectations, delegating workstreams, coaching PM I/APMs, and reinforcing disciplined project management practices.
Self-motivated to work through complex problems and competing priorities, including a high level of detail and organization.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Money as a Service (MaaS) oversees a diverse portfolio of Stripe's core products and platforms, and our vision is to become the financial operating system for platforms and marketplaces globally.. These offerings facilitate the global movement and management of funds for users. The teams that fall under the MaaS umbrella are Connect, Money Management, and Crypto. Together, these teams work to ensure Stripe users have the robust financial infrastructure and tools they need to power their businesses on a global scale.

What you’ll do

As a TPM, you will play a key role leading complex programs across multiple engineering, product and cross-functional (finance, legal, compliance, risk, and other) teams spanning Stripe. You will be responsible for the successful definition, cross-functional strategy, planning and execution of large-scale technical programs that help to solve complex problems and empower Stripe and our users.

Responsibilities

Drive functional and technical delivery of key team and org-wide programs/initiatives.
Partner with Engineering Managers, Product Managers and other cross functional partners to define, scope, and drive large programs to conclusion.
Develop, implement, and iterate on program management techniques, frameworks, and KPIs to achieve goals with well defined success criteria.
Make substantial improvements to how the teams you work with communicate and operate to significantly increase the productivity and efficiency of the teams.
Define and produce high quality written proposals, communications and documentation.
Leverage data and acquired knowledge to drive strategic decisions at an engineering leadership level.
Create widely circulated plans, driving consistency, clarity and building alignment across teams.
Help influence peers / leaders and build consensus while dealing with ambiguity.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

6+ years of software engineering, systems engineering and/or technical program management experience.
Excellent analytical skills; you digest complex information and make recommendations.
You have a track record of providing program management during all phases of software development from kick-off to launch, demonstrating critical thinking, challenging the norms and thought leadership.
You have very strong written and verbal communication skills, building strong relationships with stakeholders, teams and senior leaders around the organization.
You can drive internal and external process improvements across multiple teams and functions and bring a wealth of experience, opinions, proposals and best practices.
Experience operating autonomously and leading large-scale efforts across multiple teams and functions, with stakeholders in different disciplines across time zones.
Ability to understand how functionality comes together (across products and platforms) to deliver value for users, and identify/mitigate delivery risks proactively; can propose and drive a technical solution
Users-first and customer-focused mindset

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience in a global FinTech or banking organization

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Stripes on the Works in Progress team based in the London, UK office also work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual salary range for this role in the primary location is RON 244,800 - RON 367,200. This range may change if you are hired in another location. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings (“OTE”) range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and specific location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the primary location may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Specific benefits and details about what compensation is included in the salary range listed above will vary depending on the applicant’s location and can be discussed in more detail during the interview process. Benefits/additional compensation for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; retirement plans; health benefits; and wellness stipends.

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The Software Quality Operations (SWQOps) team is at the heart of ensuring the safety, reliability, and quality of the Waymo Driver. Our mission is to build an adaptable and scalable operation, increasingly powered by AI, to deliver the crucial insights necessary to confidently deploy and grow Waymo's autonomous vehicle service.

Why This Team Is Essential To Waymo's Success

Waymo is undergoing unprecedented growth, rapidly expanding into new cities (targeting ~20 new cities by EOY 2026) and launching new vehicle platforms. SWQ Ops plays a critical role in this expansion, making it possible to scale safely and efficiently. The Regulatory Reporting Operations team within SWQ Ops owns the scaled delivery of datasets and methodologies used to evaluate events of regulatory interest and ensure reporting accuracy as Waymo continues to scale. We are on the front lines of:

De-risking New Deployments: Through meticulous triage of driving and simulated events, issue discovery, and continuous field monitoring, SWQ Ops provides early warnings and critical insights. This "early intervention in RO issue detection" ensures operational resilience and safety, particularly in new and complex environments, which is critical as Waymo enters multiple new cities and ramps up platforms like Ojai.
Enabling International RO & Market Expansion: Our team is deeply integrated into every stage of Waymo's market entry framework, from initial city evaluation (OK2Plan) to scaling operations (OK2Scale). We provide the necessary data analysis, policy development, and quality assurance to unblock critical milestones, preventing slowdowns in market expansion velocity.
Data Flywheel: Supporting the development of a single, automated, end-to-end machine learning flywheel for the entire Waymo Driver. A successful flywheel will be the core engine for scaling our technology, enabling faster international expansion, quicker remediation of driving issues, and a significant reduction in the engineering effort required to maintain and improve the driver.
Driving Engineering Velocity: By handling the vital work of performance evaluation, issue deep-dives, and data set curation, SWQOps collaborates heavily and allows Waymo's Engineering, SysEng, Simulation, and Data Science teams to focus on their core tasks of developing and improving the Waymo Driver.
Workflow Incubation & Development: Incubating high-impact workflows and ensuring readiness for automation and long-term operational excellence.

You Will

Drive outcomes for large and complex technical operations programs that span multiple organizations. Develop and drive execution on strategic roadmaps, own forecasting and resource planning.

Bachelor's degree in technical, legal or business discipline
10+ years of experience managing complex, tech-enabled operations and experience working across cross-functional partners (Legal, Product, Engineering, Data Science, Systems Engineering) to drive outcomes
5+ years of people management experience
Experience in Regulatory Compliance, Vehicle Qualification, or similar domains, and ability to assess and operationalize legal reporting requirements

Ability to thrive in a high ambiguity, dynamic environment

Experience within A / V space

Experience with Lean / Six Sigma process improvement methodologies

Health, dental, vision, life, disability insurance

new_jobs.description:
Correlation One Develops Workforce Skills For The AI Economy

Enterprises and governments work with us to develop talent and close critical data, digital, and technology skills gaps. Our global programs, including training programs and data competitions, also empower underrepresented communities and accelerate careers.

Our mission is to create equal access to the data-driven jobs of the future. We partner with top employers and government organizations to make that a reality, including Amazon, Coca-Cola, Johnson & Johnson, the U.S. State Department, and the U.S. Department of Defense.

Our skills training programs are 100% free for learners and are delivered virtually by industry experts to minimize traditional barriers to career advancement. We take pride in fostering supportive, human-led, group learning environments that build technical proficiency and confidence in participants.

Join us and let's shape the AI Economy together!

Your Impact

As Program Manager (PM) at Correlation One, you will contribute to the success of our live, online training programs by managing key aspects of program delivery and supporting the Program Operations team in strategic initiatives. You will play a crucial role in the preparation, launch, and ongoing management of training programs, ensuring effective collaboration across teams and exceptional customer service.

The ideal candidate is an excellent project and program manager and is able to execute simultaneous competing deadlines and tasks involving multiple stakeholders. This role will support the preparation and launch of Correlation One training programs, including application setup and management, instructional staff hiring, cross-functional team collaboration, and client communication.

Reporting to a Senior Program Manager, this position requires a motivated individual with program management experience. A successful PM is a quick learner with a strong work ethic who takes initiative and is able to navigate ambiguity productively and patiently. They have an interest in changing lives through education and a desire to work on larger and/or different programs as we continue to scale. Correlation One is a company where creativity, initiative, collaboration, and communication are valued.

Key Responsibilities

Program Management
Assist in the preparation and launch of training programs, handling application setup, client communications, and managing instructional staff hiring processes.
Oversee multiple programs simultaneously, managing project timelines and ensuring seamless execution.
Support the Senior Operations Team in developing and implementing strategic initiatives to enhance program impact, experience, and scalability.
Facilitate a successful admissions process, which includes application setup and launch, applicant pipeline monitoring and reporting, and marketing initiatives, Q&A sessions, and/or any necessary applicant support to ensure strong enrollment.
Manage the instructional contractor screening, review, and hiring processes for Teaching Assistants and Lead Instructors.
Manage the live, online training programs (typically 12-20 weeks in length), ensuring learners, teaching assistants, instructors, and other stakeholders engage and benefit from the program.
Monitor learners’ progress in the course while providing support for instructors and other contractual staff.
Ensure stakeholders are fulfilling their role’s responsibilities and course technology is functioning appropriately.
Create a friendly, professional learning environment by troubleshooting learner needs and responding to all inquiries in a timely, professional manner.
Admissions Process:
Contribute to a successful admissions process, including application setup, monitoring applicant pipelines, responding to Zendesk inquiries, and participating in marketing initiatives.
Work collaboratively with the Senior Program Manager on Q&A sessions and applicant support to ensure strong enrollment.
Team Leadership and Development:
Manage and provide guidance to a small team of 1-2 Operations Analysts.
Foster a collaborative and innovative team culture, encouraging continuous learning and development.
Provide ongoing feedback, career development, and mentorship to team members.
Client Relationship Management:
Support the Senior Program Manager in cultivating and strengthening relationships with clients, ensuring their unique needs are met.
Collaborate with the Senior Program Manager to address client concerns and identify opportunities for program enhancements.
Cross-functional Collaboration:
Collaborate with various teams, including Business Operations, Curriculum, Professional Development, Account Management, and others, to ensure coordinated program execution.
Provide input to drive improvements in the overall training program ecosystem.
Strategic Insight and Reporting:
Contribute to the analysis of program performance metrics and provide insights to senior leadership.
Assist in reporting on program developments, successes, and challenges, contributing to data-driven decision-making processes.
Continuous Improvement:
Identify opportunities for process optimization and innovation, driving continuous improvement in program delivery and experience.
Implement best practices and lessons learned from previous programs to enhance overall effectiveness.

Your Expertise

Bachelor's degree preferred; Master’s degree in a relevant field is a plus.
3-5 years of experience in program management, with at least 1 directly in an educational or training institution.
Experience leading and managing teams, demonstrating autonomy and success.
Proficient in Google Suite, MS Office Suite, Slack, and Zoom.
Experience with Data analysis, CRM or Salesforce, and other education-related software is a plus.

Time Commitment

While we provide a lot of flexibility as a remote-first organization, and given the general needs of the training operations team, the guide for working hours align to the East Coast (Monday - Friday, 9AM - 6PM ET)
Given the nature of adult learners, occasional work on Saturdays is required. Compensatory time off is provided for this work.

Location:

Due to upcoming program geography, our strong preference for this Program Manager's location is Canada.

Insurance or subsidies based on country

Company-paid holidays
Official company-wide holiday for the last week of the calendar year
Access to free data skills training through our programs
A company culture that empowers individuals and embraces diversity through its core mission

new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Octant is a clinical-stage drug discovery company developing correctors for protein misfolding diseases. We are a well-backed team of experienced scientists and entrepreneurs at the frontiers of biology, chemistry, and computation, combining high-throughput synthetic biology, generative chemistry, and AI/ML to repeatedly develop precision medicines for genetically defined diseases.

JOB DESCRIPTION
We are looking for an experienced program manager to keep Octant's first program in the clinic moving on time and on budget. OCT-980, our first-in-human oral corrector for RHO-associated autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa, is currently in a Phase 1/2 trial. As program manager, you will own the integrated plan across all functional workstreams, keep the team aligned on timelines, budget, risks, and decisions and ensure program activities are coordinated and communicated to stakeholders.
Octant takes a novel, technology-forward approach to drug development, so there isn’t a standard playbook to follow. This role offers the opportunity to bring structure and rigor to a fast-moving team that's charting its own course. The program manager will report to the Chief Medical Officer.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Develop and maintain the integrated program plan, partnering with Development Team stakeholders to pressure-test and optimize the program execution timeline Clinical Development (including enrollment, site activation, database lock, and the final study report) and aligning it with CMC, drug supply, nonclinical, regulatory, and finance workstreams.
Identify critical path activities and cross-functional interdependencies, and work with workstream owners to resolve rate-limiting steps.
Develop and manage the program budget in partnership with Finance, anticipating changes in cost or timing.
Support the management of program resources including CROs, vendors, and consultants, tracking deliverables, milestones, and spend against contracts and budget.
Gather cross-functional input from clinical development, drug supply, nonclinical, and other functions to support leadership decision-making.
Maintain program risk and decision logs, with clear mitigation plans and escalation as needed.
Plan, facilitate, and document core and program team meetings, and communicate program status, milestones, and risks to senior leadership.
Work effectively across a matrixed team, influencing without direct authority and gathering information from stakeholders proactively.

THIS JOB MIGHT BE GREAT FOR YOU IF YOU HAVE:
Ideally 10 years of project or program management experience in life sciences; minimum of 5 years. Experience across the clinical development stages is a plus.
Experience on complex therapeutic programs (e.g., immunology, oncology) is preferred; ophthalmology experience is ideal.
A track record of building and maintaining integrated plans across functions, and of delivering programs on time and within budget.
Experience tracking program budgets, partnering with Finance, and managing contracts and vendors such as CROs.
The ability to work effectively across scientific, clinical, technical, and financial domains, and to communicate clearly, proactively, and collaboratively with stakeholders at every level.
Comfort with changing priorities, and the ability to anticipate issues and help the team make decisions before they become critical.
A Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline or a related field; an advanced degree is a plus. Equivalent experience can substitute for formal degree programs.
PMP or program management training is a plus; strong analytical, conflict-resolution, and communication skills are essential.

The expected annual salary for this role is in the range of $150,000 to $185,000, depending on experience level. We offer health benefits (medical, dental, vision), equity, and 401(k) matching.

Octant is located in Emeryville, California and our team works onsite.

Octant is an equal opportunity company that values applicants of all backgrounds. We're committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive work environment. We value less traditional backgrounds, and may consider an equivalent combination of knowledge, skills, education, and experience to meet minimum qualifications. We know that confidence-gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting spectacular candidates, so please don't hesitate to apply — we'd love to hear from you.

new_jobs.description:
KIOXIA America, Inc. (formerly Toshiba Memory America, Inc.) is the US-based subsidiary of KIOXIA Corporation, a leading worldwide supplier of flash memory and solid state drives (SSDs). From the invention of flash memory to today’s breakthrough BiCS FLASH™ 3D technology, KIOXIA continues to pioneer cutting-edge memory solutions and services that enrich people's lives and expand society's horizons. The company's innovative 3D flash memory technology, BiCS FLASH™, is shaping the future of storage in high-density applications, including advanced smartphones, PCs, SSDs, automotive and data centers.

Job Description

KIOXIA America is seeking a Senior Staff Technical Program Manager to join the SSD Business Unit Program Management Office (PMO). This senior individual-contributor role will provide program leadership for highly complex and business-critical SSD product development initiatives from product definition through development, qualification, high-volume manufacturing, customer readiness, sustaining, and end of life. The Senior Staff Technical Program Manager will be based within KIOXIA America and serve as a senior cross-functional program leader between the U.S. organization and KIOXIA’s global headquarters in Japan, bringing together Engineering, Firmware, Validation, Quality & Reliability, Product Line Management, Technical Product Management, Customer Technical Support, Business Development, Operations, and other stakeholders. The role is accountable for driving execution across organizational boundaries, including integrated schedules, critical paths, dependencies, program risks, decisions, actions, and escalations. The successful candidate will combine strong SSD technical knowledge with advanced program and organizational leadership. They will operate independently in complex and ambiguous environments, anticipate program-level risks and dependencies, understand how decisions across hardware, firmware, NAND, controller/ASIC, validation, qualification, manufacturing, and customer enablement affect overall program execution, and influence cross-functional and senior leaders to achieve predictable business outcomes.

Responsibilities

Own end-to-end execution of highly complex and business-critical SSD programs, potentially spanning multiple development teams, customer requirements, or significant technical dependencies.
Serve as a senior cross-functional program leader, establishing alignment on objectives, priorities, execution strategy, success criteria, lifecycle gates, and exit criteria.
Build and govern integrated program schedules covering key milestones, critical paths, functional dependencies, development builds, qualification, customer readiness, and manufacturing deliverables.
Anticipate significant program risks and cross-functional dependencies and drive mitigation or recovery strategies before they materially affect program commitments.
Lead resolution of complex technical and business tradeoffs involving scope, architecture, resources, quality, schedule, customer requirements, and business priorities.
Establish and lead effective Core Team operating mechanisms focused on program health, critical decisions, milestones, actions, risks, dependencies, and escalation.
Drive accountability across functional and organizational boundaries for agreed deliverables, milestones, decisions, actions, and commitments.
Provide clear, fact-based program assessments, recommendations, decision options, and escalation information to functional and senior management.
Coordinate effectively between KIOXIA America and KIOXIA’s global headquarters in Japan, influencing stakeholders across organizations, geographies, technical disciplines, and time zones.
Drive product development and qualification readiness across SSD builds, firmware maturity, validation, issue resolution, manufacturing, and customer qualification dependencies.
Resolve complex or ambiguous blockers and drive high-impact decisions toward closure with clear owners, dates, rationale, and measurable outcomes.
Partner with PMO, engineering, and product leadership to implement and improve program governance, lifecycle/gate processes, integrated planning, dashboards, decision mechanisms, and execution practices.
Identify recurring execution gaps and lead cross-functional improvements that strengthen program predictability, efficiency, accountability, and transparency.
Provide guidance and share best practices with other technical program managers and cross-functional team members, helping strengthen program-management discipline across the organization.
Champion data-driven program management and automation to improve program visibility, identify emerging schedule or risk changes, and reduce manual status reporting.
Capture and apply lessons learned to improve execution across current and future programs.

Qualifications

10+ years of related experience with a Bachelor’s; 10+ years of experience with a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 10+ years of experience in a technical field.
10+ years of experience in complex hardware/software product development, semiconductor, storage, memory, or an equivalent technical product environment.
Significant technical program or project leadership experience delivering complex, business-critical product development and New Product Introduction programs.
Demonstrated experience leading programs spanning multiple organizations, technical disciplines, dependencies, and senior stakeholders.
Advanced ability to build and govern integrated schedules, critical paths, dependencies, risk management plans, milestones, and recovery strategies.
Strong understanding of SSD architecture and development, including controller/ASIC, NAND, DRAM, firmware, hardware, validation, qualification, reliability, manufacturing, and customer enablement.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and lead highly matrixed cross-functional teams without direct reporting authority.
Proven ability to frame and drive complex decisions, work through ambiguity, and balance technical, customer, resource, quality, business, and schedule considerations.
Strong systems thinking and analytical problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify risks, patterns, and dependencies across major program workstreams.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including management-level program assessments, recommendations, decision framing, and escalation.
Experience working with geographically distributed teams; experience coordinating between a U.S. organization and global headquarters in Japan is highly valued.
Experience with modern program tracking, analytics, and dashboard tools such as Jira and Power BI or equivalent platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience leading enterprise or data-center SSD product development and qualification programs of significant complexity.
Experience with SSD New Product Introduction, development build planning, qualification, transition to high-volume manufacturing, and customer deployment.
Strong familiarity with semiconductor product lifecycles and vertically integrated development environments.
Experience implementing and improving PMO operating mechanisms, governance, lifecycle gates, integrated planning, and management reporting.
Experience providing guidance to program managers and influencing execution practices across cross-functional teams.
Track record of identifying recurring organizational or execution challenges and leading practical cross-functional improvements.
Ability to use data-driven automation and reporting to surface exceptions, schedule movement, dependencies, and emerging risks.

Quantifind is the Risk Intelligence company. We help some of the world’s biggest banks identify money laundering and fraud. Quantifind also works with government agencies, using the same platform, to uncover criminal networks and support national security. Unlike other players in this space, Quantifind delivers results through an AI-driven software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution with consumer-grade user experiences.

Quantifind’s Graphyte platform uncovers signals of risk across disparate and unstructured text sources using artificial intelligence and natural language processing techniques. In financial crimes risk management, Quantifind’s solution uniquely combines internal financial institution data with public domain data to assess risk in the context of Know Your Customer (KYC), Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Fraud Risk Management, and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) processes. Today these compliance processes are burdened by ever-increasing regulatory responsibilities and an expectation of frictionless transactions. Legacy technologies demand increasingly more human resources as the operations expand; Quantifind’s solution offers a way to cut through the inefficiency and enhance effectiveness simultaneously. Demand for this solution is fueling our rapid growth.

To help you succeed, we provide a supportive environment that fosters collaboration between teams and team members, where learning and professional growth are considered a key part of your success, and of ours. We offer a flexible work environment with a family friendly work-life balance.

new_jobs.description:
True Zero Technologies, a veteran-owned small business, was founded on the principle that the purposeful enablement of people and technology in an organization directly ties to the quality of its outcomes. True Zero recognizes that those outcomes begin and end with our people, and that is what we have built a community of like-minded, driven, and passionate individuals and innovators who are aligned in a common goal of delivering top-tier services to our customers. Our culture and commitment have been recognized through numerous accolades, including being named one of the Best Places to Work
in 2023 in two categories (“Prosperous and Thriving” ($5MM–$50MM in gross revenue) and “Mid-Atlantic Region” (DC, DE, MD, NC, VA, WV)), and again in 2025 as a Best Places to Work
honoree. In addition, True Zero earned coveted spots on the Inc. 5000
list of fastest-growing companies in America in 2022, 2023, and 2025
, a testament to our sustained growth driven by our people-first approach and unwavering dedication to excellence.

True Zero Technologies is seeking a Senior Cybersecurity IT Program Manager to provide senior-level program management, technical leadership, and strategic guidance in support of enterprise cybersecurity and information technology initiatives. This position is responsible for overseeing the successful planning, execution, delivery, and continuous improvement of complex cybersecurity programs while ensuring alignment with customer mission objectives, regulatory requirements, and enterprise security strategies.

The Senior Cybersecurity IT Program Manager will serve as a trusted advisor to government and commercial stakeholders, bridging technical and business requirements, managing cross-functional teams, and driving the implementation of mission-critical cybersecurity capabilities that deliver measurable outcomes and improve the customer’s overall security posture.

Job Responsibilities

Cybersecurity Program Management: Lead the full lifecycle of complex cybersecurity and IT programs, including initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, controlling, and closeout, ensuring alignment with established scope, schedule, budget, quality, and performance objectives.
Strategic Planning and Roadmap Development: Develop and maintain cybersecurity program strategies, implementation roadmaps, operational frameworks, and investment priorities that align with customer mission objectives and enterprise security requirements.
Technical Leadership and Solution Delivery: Provide technical oversight and strategic guidance supporting the design, development, and implementation of secure enterprise architectures, cybersecurity solutions, and mission-critical technology capabilities.
Program Governance and Performance Management: Establish program governance structures, performance metrics, key performance indicators (KPIs), milestones, and reporting mechanisms to measure program effectiveness, track deliverables, and communicate progress to customer stakeholders.
Risk Management and Regulatory Compliance: Identify, assess, track, and mitigate program risks, issues, dependencies, and resource constraints while ensuring cybersecurity initiatives align with applicable frameworks, standards, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements.
Stakeholder Management and Executive Communication: Serve as a primary liaison between customer stakeholders, executive leadership, technical teams, and program personnel, providing strategic recommendations, status updates, executive briefings, and actionable guidance.
Resource Management and Team Leadership: Coordinate cross-functional cybersecurity and IT teams, manage resource allocation and competing priorities, mentor technical and program personnel, and promote collaboration, innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Program Management, or a related field.
Minimum of seven (7) years of professional experience in cybersecurity, information technology, technical program management, or related enterprise technology disciplines, with demonstrated experience managing complex cybersecurity or IT programs.
Demonstrated experience managing the full program and project lifecycle, including scope, schedule, budget, resource allocation, risk management, deliverables, and performance reporting.
Strong understanding of enterprise cybersecurity technologies and operational functions, including security operations, incident response, identity and access management, vulnerability management, cloud security, Zero Trust, and network security.
Experience managing cross-functional technical teams and coordinating multiple concurrent projects, workstreams, dependencies, and stakeholder requirements within complex enterprise environments.
Knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks, regulatory requirements, and industry standards, including NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), NIST SP 800-53, Risk Management Framework (RMF), and FISMA.
Experience developing program management plans, integrated master schedules, cybersecurity roadmaps, risk registers, performance dashboards, executive briefings, and program status reports.
Demonstrated experience applying Agile, Scrum, Waterfall, or hybrid program and project management methodologies.
Strong leadership, analytical, financial management, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into actionable business and mission outcomes.

Preferred Requirements

Relevant industry certifications such as Project Management Professional (PMP), Program Management Professional (PgMP), Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), or PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP).
Experience managing federal government cybersecurity or IT programs, including contract deliverables, performance work statements (PWS), service-level agreements (SLAs), financial performance, and customer reporting requirements.
Experience managing enterprise cybersecurity modernization initiatives, including Zero Trust implementation, cloud security transformation, security operations modernization, and enterprise security architecture initiatives.
Experience utilizing program management and reporting technologies such as Microsoft Project, Jira, Confluence, ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, Power BI, or similar enterprise platforms.

About The Job

gTech's Extended Workforce Solutions (xWS) team empowers Product Areas (PAs) to optimize outsourced operations while reducing risks and driving efficiency through the enforcement of Google best practices and policies. We advocate for informed decision-making, ensuring our partners find the right talent in the right locations. Our collaboration across Google leads to streamlined processes, minimizing administrative burdens and optimizing the extended workforce (xW) experience. We ensure Google's policies and guidelines are consistently adhered to.

The Risk and Compliance (R&C) team within xWS is responsible for ensuring that Google complies with all laws and regulations applicable to its contingent workforce globally. The team does this by identifying and assessing risks, setting requirements, designing and assessing controls, ensuring governance, and conducting testing and auditing. R&C equips, enables, and empowers Googlers to achieve success while protecting Google's brand and reputation. The team is a second line of defence at Google, working with other teams to ensure that Google is compliant with all applicable laws and regulations.

As a Risk Program Manager in xWS you will be at the forefront of enabling Google’s business to scale safely. In this role, you will help shift and drive the compliance narrative to responsible, strategic enablement at enterprise scale.

Operating as a key player in our Second Line of Defense (2LOD), you will architect the risk frameworks that allow next-generation workflows to scale with speed and confidence, owning the end-to-end lifecycle of risk management, from risk identification and control design to continuous monitoring and executive reporting and embed governance, risk, and compliance principles across the lifecycle.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Ireland: €112000 - €114000 (EUR) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Standardize xWS risk taxonomies, registers, assessment methodologies, and acceptance criteria to operationalize and mature extended workforce processes and system integrations.
Design calibrated guardrails for emerging AI operations, agentic workflows, and non-traditional workforce delivery models, executing end-to-end Alphabet-wide risk and control assessments.
Partner with business teams to embed compliance-by-design controls into fast-paced operational pipelines, mitigating legal, regulatory, and critical operational risks.
Build KRI dashboards for continuous risk telemetry, using upstream predictors to identify vulnerabilities and synthesizing complex metrics into structured executive narratives.

new_jobs.description:
Role Description

Cyber Recovery Project Manager Sr. – Exercises

The Role

Lead the planning, execution, and continuous improvement of enterprise Cyber Recovery exercises, ensuring critical infrastructure, applications, dependencies, recovery playbooks, and decision-making processes are validated against realistic cyber-disruption scenarios. This supports the current Cyber Recovery operating model, which includes exercise execution and resolution of issues identified through exercises.

What You’ll Do

Exercise Program Management: Own the end-to-end exercise lifecycle, including scope, objectives, scenarios, schedules, participants, dependencies, execution, and reporting.
Scenario & Exercise Planning: Coordinate realistic ransomware/destructive-event tabletop, simulation, and technical recovery exercises across infrastructure, cloud, security, and application teams.
Recovery Playbook Validation: Validate recovery playbooks for completeness, technical accuracy, usability, recovery sequencing, and actionable restoration steps.
Dependency & RTO/RPO Validation: Ensure exercises test critical dependencies such as DNS, DHCP, Identity, network, storage/backup, databases, cloud, and application services before broader restoration. These dependencies are specifically identified in the current Cyber Recovery assessment scope.
Cross-Functional Coordination: Drive participation across Cyber Recovery, Infrastructure, Public Cloud, Information Security, Application teams, Operations, Incident Response, business stakeholders, and vendors.
Exercise Execution & Facilitation: Manage exercise logistics, injects, decision points, technical recovery activities, escalations, and stakeholder communications.
After-Action Reviews: Produce exercise results, lessons learned, gaps, bottlenecks, and recommendations, leveraging findings across successive exercises to identify recurring weaknesses.
Remediation Tracking: Convert exercise findings into actionable remediation plans with owners, priorities, target dates, risks, and closure criteria.
Metrics & Reporting: Maintain exercise dashboards and KPIs covering readiness, participation, recovery performance, RTO/RPO attainment, findings, remediation aging, and overall program maturity.
Audit & Compliance Support: Maintain exercise evidence and documentation to demonstrate recovery readiness and support Internal Audit, regulatory, and risk-management requirements. The Cyber Recovery model specifically embeds audit readiness and remediation tracking into ongoing operations.

This position description identifies the responsibilities and tasks typically associated with the performance of the position. Other relevant essential functions may be required.

IT Project Manager

The Opportunity:

As an IT Project Manager, you know the complexities of supporting a project from concept to completion. Many programs require a significant investment of limited resources, and it’s imperative to keep the project on a productive path. That’s why we need you, an experienced IT Project Manager who can help ensure success through careful analysis and effective communication. You’ll help with tactical planning using resources like Microsoft tools and regular interactions with SMEs, technical directors, engineers, and contracting officers.

The real impact of project management comes from communication to ensure the program achieves its goals and meets our quality standards. At Booz Allen, we recognize that we must continuously grow as a team to bring the best support to our clients, so here you’ll have all the resources to succeed. This is a chance to influence a meaningful mission while learning how to develop and maintain program strategy. Work with us and ensure our customer accomplishes its program goals within budget as we improve warfighter communications.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

5+ years of experience supporting and managing IT, software development, or cybersecurity projects from planning through delivery
Experience with engineering, including in network and systems security, authentication, access controls, vulnerability scanning, and security baselines
Experience applying Agile and Scrum or standard SDLC workflows to guide sprint tasks, unblock daily technical work, and keep milestones on schedule
Experience serving as an advisor to upper-level management
Experience planning, coordinating, and developing comprehensive reports to improve the overall development and execution of organizational programs
Ability to coordinate effectively across engineering teams, internal stakeholders, and external partners and explain technical issues clearly to non-engineers
Active TS/SCI clearance; willingness to take a polygraph exam
Associate’s degree and 5+ years of experience supporting IT projects and activities, Bachelor’s degree and 3+ years of experience supporting IT projects and activities, or Master’s degree and 1+ years of experience supporting IT projects and activities
Ability to obtain a DoD 8570 IAT Level II Certification, including Security+ CE, CCNA-Security, GSEC, SSCP, CySA+, GICSP, or CND Certification within 30 days of start date
Ability to obtain a DoD 8570.01-M Cybersecurity Service Provider - Infrastructure Support Certification such as CEH, CHFI, CFR, Cloud+, or CND Certification within 30 days of start date

Experience capturing technical requirements, writing standard operating procedures (SOPs), tracking action items, and preparing clear regular status reports
Experience conducting quantitative or qualitative analysis and evaluation of programs and providing management with information about improving initiatives and strategic plans
Experience creating project management plans

About the Role

AppGate Professional Services is looking for a customer-focused Customer Delivery Project Manager to lead the implementation of our Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) platform for US commercial customers. As the primary customer-facing lead for medium to large engagements, typically two to six months long, you will own delivery from project handover through production go-live and transition to Support and Customer Success.
This is a delivery leadership role, not a sales or account management position. You will manage scope, schedule, budget, deliverables, and expectations across structured, milestone-driven projects, working alongside AppGate engineers so they can stay focused on architecture, configuration, and customer enablement. Professional Services operates as a P&L, so this role directly influences project profitability, revenue realization, and services margin. Success is measured by on-time milestone delivery, customer satisfaction at go-live and close-out, project financial performance, and clean handover to Support with complete close-out documentation.

Key Responsibilities

Customer and Stakeholder Management

•Serve as the primary AppGate point of contact for US commercial customers throughout service delivery, managing day-to-day requests and communication.

Financial Accountability (P&L)

•Own the financial health of assigned projects, including hours burned against contracted hours, utilization, and billing accuracy.
•Identify revenue, margin, and schedule risk early; flag burn-rate deviations and propose corrective action before budget is exceeded.
•Drive timely milestone completion and customer sign-off to support accurate billing and revenue realization.
•Protect services margin by preventing unbilled scope: no out-of-scope work proceeds without an approved change order.

Delivery Quality and Governance

•Apply AppGate's global delivery methodology consistently across engagements.

•Experience managing complex B2B technology implementations.
•Demonstrated ability to manage scope, schedule, budget, and stakeholder expectations across structured, milestone-driven commercial IT or security projects.

– EY
Bologna

Perché candidarsi in EY?

Lo abbiamo chiesto a chi ci lavora già! Questi i fattori più influenti:

Investimento sulle competenze del futuro: fin dal primo giorno, eventi, strumenti e corsi sull’Intelligenza Artificiale, disponibili per tutti;
Formazione continua: oltre 50 ore di corsi tecnici e manageriali all’anno previsti per ciascuna persona;
Sviluppo e progressione di carriera: solo negli ultimi 12 mesi, oltre la metà delle persone di EY si è vista riconoscere un avanzamento di carriera;

Lavoro ibrido senza giornate prestabilite centralmente.
Un network internazionale su cui poter contare.

gestire progetti IT complessi end-to-end, dalla raccolta dei requisiti alla pianificazione, execution e delivery, garantendo il presidio di tempi, costi, rischi, milestone e qualità.
analizzare esigenze e requisiti IT traducendoli in priorità progettuali e valutandone gli impatti sul business.
predisporre project plan, status report, KPI e documentazione di governance.
coordinare team multidisciplinari, assicurando un efficace allineamento tra stakeholder di business e interlocutori IT.

Almeno 3 anni di esperienza in attività di gestione di progetti IT complessi, preferibilmente maturata in contesti consulenziali o su progetti rivolti a clienti.
Laurea magistrale, preferibilmente in discipline ingegneristiche, economiche, informatiche o affini
Conoscenza delle principali metodologie di Project Management, sia Agile che Waterfall, e dei principali framework, come Scrum
Buone capacità analitiche, organizzative e di problem solving.
Ottime capacità comunicative e attitudine al lavoro in squadra.
Conoscenza della lingua inglese a livello avanzato.

In EY potrai:

Accelerare le tue competenze: Grazie a corsi e programmi di sviluppo orientati al futuro, utilizzando tecnologie smart e applicazioni AI che ti liberano dalle attività ripetitive: da Copilot365 al tool proprietario EYQ, passando per PowerBI
Allargare i tuoi orizzonti: Lavora in team internazionali, disponendo di un network di professionisti globali
Dare il meglio di te: Investi costantemente nel tuo benessere personale e nello sviluppo della tua carriera, con una figura di Counselor che ti supporta dal primo giorno.

Avrai infine l’opportunità di:

accedere a benefits e programmi di welfare aziendale diversificati;
partecipare a programmi di leadership.

Per la presente posizione è previsto un range retributivo compreso tra 33.000€ e 44.000€, definito sulla base di criteri oggettivi e neutri rispetto al genere. Il rapporto di lavoro è regolato dal CCNL Commercio; il livello di inquadramento contrattuale e collettivo e la relativa disciplina applicabile saranno determinati in coerenza con l’esperienza e il profilo professionale della risorsa inserita nel processo di selezione.

In EY crediamo che ciascuna persona porti con sé qualcosa di unico:

Le tue esperienze, ambizioni e prospettive contribuiscono a creare un ambiente in cui l’unicità di ognuno diventa la nostra forza collettiva. Promuoviamo una cultura inclusiva
, dove tutte le voci sono ascoltate e valorizzate: Together, all in.
